title: Composite-signal strategy and rollback heuristics for Optimize evals
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: PRD and acceptance criteria for a composite evaluation signal used by Optimize to decide A/B winners, canary progression, and automated rollback triggers. Focus: prompt set stratification, per-metric regression thresholds, composite scoring, statistical test settings, and severity-tiered rollback heuristics.
background: Optimize currently emits per-prompt and per-metric deltas for candidate model changes but lacks a standardized composite decision pipeline and actionable rollback rules. PMs and SREs need a repeatable, explainable mechanism so quality regressions are caught early without excessive false positives that block safe rollouts.
goals: Define a composite signal that aggregates semantic quality, safety, latency, and cost into a single actionable score
Specify A/B test parameters (alpha, power, effect sizes) to use across canary sizes
Create tiered rollback triggers (soft alert -> pause -> auto-rollback) with explicit numeric thresholds and aging rules
Produce acceptance criteria and test harness to validate the gating logic before shipping
non_goals: Model-selection heuristics (e.g., choose quantization level) rather than eval gating
Replace human-in-the-loop reviews for ambiguous safety regressions
Support multi-armed bandits in this initial rollout (out of scope)
constraints: Must integrate with existing Optimize telemetry (promptset labels, metric time series, dashboards). Statistical tests need to run within 30 minutes of canary batch completion. Implementation must not add >10% overhead to existing eval job runtimes.
user_stories: As a PM, I want a single pass/fail decision and the rationale so I can approve or stop a rollout
As an SRE, I want automated rollback for severe latency regressions to avoid customer impact
As an engineer, I want reproducible test parameters so we can reproduce gating outcomes in PRs and postmortems
requirements: R1: Prompt set stratification — each eval run must include labeled prompt cohorts: core-functional, edge-cases, safety-sensitive, localization. Minimum 200 samples per cohort for canary sizes >=1k requests.

R2: Metrics computed per-cohort — for every cohort compute: quality_score (0-100), safety_violations_per_1k, median_latency_ms, cost_per_1k_tokens. Quality_score is a weighted BLEU+ROUGE+semantic-similarity signal using model-validated embeddings.

R3: Composite score — implement a normalized weighted sum: composite = w_q*delta_quality - w_s*delta_safety_penalty - w_l*delta_latency_z - w_c*delta_cost_z. Default weights: w_q=0.6, w_s=0.25, w_l=0.1, w_c=0.05. Weights must be configurable per-project.

R4: Statistical tests — default A/B significance level alpha=0.01 for safety metrics, alpha=0.05 for quality; use two-sided bootstrap for quality_score and Poisson tests for safety counts. Minimum detectable effect (MDE) guidance included in docs.

R5: Rollout policy — define three severity tiers: SEV-3 (informational), SEV-2 (pause rollout, require human review), SEV-1 (auto-rollback). Map composite score and per-metric deltas to tiers. SEV-1 triggers if safety_violations_per_1k increases by >= 30% and composite_score < -0.08 with p<0.01.

R6: Aging and transient suppression — require a regression to persist across two sequential canary batches or 12 hours (whichever longer) before SEV-1 auto-rollback unless X indicates catastrophic safety signals (see R7).

R7: Catastrophic safety bypass — single-call safety violations of severity 'blocker' (as defined by safety taxonomy) must trigger immediate SEV-1 evaluation and alerting; optional immediate rollback if human-in-the-loop disabled.

R8: Explainability outputs — each gating decision must produce: per-cohort metric deltas, composite score breakdown, statistical test p-values, sample counterexamples for failure modes (max 5), links to PR and eval run IDs.

R9: Test harness — provide a synthetic regression runner that can inject controlled deltas (quality -3 to +3 points, latency +/-50%) to validate thresholds. Acceptable false positive rate for SEV-1 on synthetic "no-change" runs: <=1% over 500 trials.
R10: Observability — events must be logged to Optimize events stream and surfaced on the per-route dashboard with 90-day retention for postmortems.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Composite scoring implemented and documented; weights can be overridden via project config and changes propagates to runs within 5 minutes

AC2: Demo canary runs (3 separate canaries) exhibit expected alarm behavior when synthetic regressions are injected: SEV-3 for small regressions, SEV-2 for medium, SEV-1 for large or sustained regressions
AC3: Statistical tests produce p-values and confidence intervals; unit tests cover edge cases (small N, zero counts) and pass in CI

AC4: Auto-rollback path exercised in staging: when safety_violations_per_1k increases >=30% with p<0.01 across two sequential canaries, rollout reverses automatically and an incident task is created linking the eval run and rollback PR
AC5: False positive rate for auto-rollback on no-change synthetic runs <=1% across a 500-trial run in staging
AC6: Post-deploy dashboard widgets created: composite score trend, per-cohort deltas, and active rollouts view; basic RBAC ensures only release approvers can override SEV-1 auto-rollback
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Spec review with ENG and SRE (2 weeks) — finalize weights and tests
Phase 1: Implement scoring and tests in staging; run synthetic harness at scale (1 week)
Phase 2: Enable soft alerts for 10% of real canaries (read-only) and collect signal concordance (2 weeks)
Phase 3: Enable pause-on-SEV-2 for 50% of canaries and require human approval before progression (2 weeks)
Phase 4: Full auto-rollback on SEV-1 with monitoring and ops playbook (1 week)
test_plan: Unit tests for composite score normalization and weight overrides
Integration tests for statistical test modules with deterministic seeds
E2E harness: synthetic regression runner (500 trials) to validate false positive/negative rates
Manual playbook run: SRE runs a controlled canary and verifies pause/rollback flows and alert routing
decisions: Use weighted-sum composite instead of more opaque ML classifier for explainability (DEC-2025-01)
Default weights chosen to prioritize quality and safety; latency/cost de-emphasized but still tracked (DEC-2025-02)
Bootstrap CI for quality metrics to handle non-normal distributions (DEC-2025-03)
open_questions: Q1: Should localization cohorts have different default weights? Proposal: yes, but defer to product owners per-market.
Q2: When TTL for suppression should be shortened for paid enterprise customers who expect faster rollouts? (ops input required)
Q3: Do we allow customers to disable auto-rollback entirely per-project? (security/enterprise sales trade-off)
